documents.notes: Carries the header 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION UNDER THE AGREED ARBITRATION PROCEDURES PREPARED FOR SETTLEMENT PURPOSES'. pages.transcript:
CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION UNDER THE AGREED ARBITRATION PROCEDURES
PREPARED FOR SETTLEMENT PURPOSES

Schwartz came to The Post in the early 1990s as a reporter in National. He became a reporter in Financial News in 1999. Prior to starting at The Post, Schwartz worked as a senior writer at Newsweek for eight years. Schwartz is a graduate of University of Texas, where he also holds a law degree.

Starting Salary
Upon starting at The Post, Schwartz received approximately a six percent increase over his prior salary. His starting salary was more than the salaries of Hamilton, Mayer and Skrzycki at that time.

Salary History
Schwartz received two merit increases during his time at The Post – both of which he received as a reporter in National.

Explanation:
Schwartz received a high salary from Newsweek, his previous employer – more than the salaries of Hamilton and Mayer at The Post at that time. Therefore, Schwartz's starting salary was also more than the salaries of Hamilton and Mayer at that time.

Schwartz's salary was a function of his work in National. His salary was not affected by any salary decisions made while he was reporter in National News.

Schwartz came to Financial News from National to cover technology policy – a rising area of importance to Financial News. Schwartz was considered one of the early experts on the Internet.

Schwartz was highly valued in the marketplace – evidenced by the lucrative offer he accepted from The New York Times.

David Segal

David Segal was paid substantially less than Hamilton on the 1995 to 1998 salary snapshots and less than Hamilton on the 1999 salary snapshot. Segal was paid substantially less than Mayer on the 1995 to 1999 salary snapshots.

Experience and Education
Segal came to The Post in the mid-1990s as an Assistant Editor in Book World. He became a reporter in Financial News in 1995. He left Financial News in 2000 to become a critic in Style where he remains today. Prior to starting at The Post, Segal worked as an Editor for the Washington Monthly for approximately two years. He also worked as a freelance writer for a little less than four years. Segal is a graduate of Harvard University and holds a Masters in Politics and Philosophy from Oxford University.

pages.transcript:
CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION UNDER THE AGREED ARBITRATION PROCEDURES
PREPARED FOR SETTLEMENT PURPOSES

Upon starting at The Post, Brown received approximately a 35 percent increase over his prior salary at the Philadelphia Inquirer. His starting salary was the same as the salary of Hamilton at that time. Mayer did not work at The Post at that time. The Post has not yet located Brown's salary at the time Mayer started at The Post in 1981. Skrzycki did not work at The Post at that time. When Skrzycki started at The Post in 1986, her salary was more than the salary of Brown at that time.

Salary History
As of September 1, 2002, Brown received five merit increases – four of which he received as a reporter in Financial News. He received these four merit increases in the following years: 1988, 1993, 1994 and 1995. Brown also received two substantial salary increases – each roughly 20 percent of his salary – in 2000 in response to competing job offers.

Explanation:
Brown has received lucrative offers from internet companies that wished to hire Brown as their car columnist. In order to keep Brown at The Post, Brown was given two approximately 20 percent salary increases in 2000.

Brown has a unique position at The Post – that of a high profile car columnist. As such, he was considered irreplaceable.

William Brubaker

William Brubaker was paid substantially more than Hamilton on the 2001 and 2002 salary snapshots. Brubaker was also paid more than Mayer and Skrzycki on the 2001 and 2002 salary snapshots. Brubaker and Walsh did not work together in Financial News at that time.

Experience and Education
Brubaker came to The Post in the mid-1980s as a reporter in Sports. He became a reporter in Financial News in 2000. Prior to starting at The Post, Brubaker worked for a little over two years as a freelance investigative reporter at Sports Illustrated. Prior to working at Sports Illustrated, Brubaker spent three years as a writer/reporter for the New York Daily News; seven years as a writer/reporter for the Miami News; and one year as a writer/reporter for the Hollywood Sun-Tattler. Brubaker is a graduate of Biscayne College.
